pattern_name: Loop-Bound Tightening for Huffman Fast Loop
variant_desc: Conservative `ilimit = src + 14` early exit forces ~14 extra slow-path iterations per decode -> `ilowest = src`: fast loop's own 7-byte/iter invariant guarantees safety without the 14-byte margin (variant 3: seed=45, n_scale=2.0x)
source_citation: zstd PR #3827 (Yann Collet 2023, 'Tighten Huffman fast loop bound'). Commit reports +28% / +30% measured speedup.
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that a defensive `ilimit = src + 14` safety margin in a Huffman fast loop is over-cautious when the loop's own invariant (7 bytes/iter from src, 4 bytes/iter to dst) already guarantees no over-read. Eliminating the margin lets the fast loop run all the way to src_end instead of dropping into the per-symbol slow path 14 bytes early -- zstd PR #3827 measured +28% / +30% on full decode pipelines. No compiler infers this because it cannot prove the loop's own bounds without symbolic execution of the encoder. NOTE: in this isolated microbenchmark we use SAFETY=180 (vs PR #3827's 14) to amplify the effect into a measurable wall-clock signal at -O3; the per-symbol slow path's cost dominates less in microbenchmarks than in a full decoder pipeline, so the at-O3 speedup hovers around 1.1-1.2x rather than the PR's 1.28x.
